misconception_description: Student believes that conditional statements, i.e., Python statements that evaluate to either True or False, must always be wrapped in if/else statements to be returned as Boolean values.

solutions.generated_code:
program HitungInversi
kamus
  a, b, c, jumlah : integer
  terbalik : boolean
algoritma
  input(a, b, c)
  jumlah <- 0
  if a > b then
    terbalik <- true
  else
    terbalik <- false
  endif
  if terbalik then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1
  endif
  if a > c then
    terbalik <- true
  else
    terbalik <- false
  endif
  if terbalik then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1
  endif
  if b > c then
    terbalik <- true
  else
    terbalik <- false
  endif
  if terbalik then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1
  endif
  output(jumlah)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student created a helper function `is_inversion` to check if two elements form an inversion. Due to their misconception that boolean expressions must be wrapped in if/else statements to return boolean values, they wrote `if val1 > val2: return True else: return False` instead of simply `return val1 > val2`. The code functions correctly but is unnecessarily verbose. From the student's perspective, this is the proper way to return a boolean value from a conditional expression.
